title: Ten slots fill up fast
hook: Ten slots, random keys. How soon do two keys land in the same slot?

knows: a list of numbered slots or boxes
that 'random' means each slot is equally likely
doesNotKnow: how a hash function picks a slot
how soon two keys share a slot

misconception: With 10 slots you can store about 10 keys before collisions become a problem.
objective: The learner can explain that with 10 slots a collision is more likely than not by the 5th key, because each new key's chance of missing all earlier keys multiplies down, so hash tables plan for collisions early.

claims.text: With 10 equally likely slots, the chance 4 keys all land in different slots is 1 x 0.9 x 0.8 x 0.7 = 0.504.
claims.source: Key k misses the k - 1 occupied slots with probability (10 - (k - 1))/10; independent keys multiply: 1 x 0.9 x 0.8 x 0.7 = 0.504. Builder computed it in Node.

claims.text: With 5 keys the chance of no collision falls to 0.3024, so a collision has about a 70% chance: 5 is the first number of keys where a collision is more likely than not.
claims.source: 0.504 x 0.6 = 0.3024; 1 - 0.3024 = 0.6976. At 4 keys the collision chance is 0.496 < 0.5. Builder computed both in Node.

claims.text: When the first collision happens at key 5, at least half the 10 slots are still empty.
claims.source: 5 keys with at least one shared slot occupy at most 4 slots, leaving at least 6 of 10 empty.

claims.text: Hash tables handle collisions on purpose, for example by keeping a short list of keys in each slot (chaining).
claims.source: CLRS 3rd ed., 11.2 'Hash tables', collision resolution by chaining.

claims.text: Java's HashMap grows its table when it is 75% full (default load factor 0.75).
claims.source: Java SE API docs, java.util.HashMap: 'the default load factor (.75) offers a good tradeoff between time and space costs'; the table is rehashed when the number of entries exceeds load factor x capacity.

claims.text: The stage's slot choices are seeded pseudo-random, so its tallies are a sample, not the exact probabilities.
claims.source: Demo.tsx slotOf(): a fixed integer mix of (table, key). Builder checked 201 seeded tables: 67.7% had a collision by key 5 (exact 69.76%), mean first collision at key 4.83.

recall.question: A hash table has 10 empty slots. You add 5 keys at random. Which is most likely?
options: No collisions: there is room for 10
recall.why: The chances of each key missing the others multiply down fast: 5 keys in 10 slots collide about 70% of the time.
